MD Admissions

Thank you for your interest in Emory School of Medicine. Below you will find all the details needed to apply to our MD programs. You can find answers on our Frequently Asked Questions page.

MD Admission FAQ
A Note to Applicants for Fall 2027

The 2026-2027 Emory Supplemental Application will open in July. In order to receive the application, your MCAT scores must meet our pre-screening criteria (see How to Apply -Step 3 for more details).

Interviews will be conducted virtually October-March. If you are selected for an interview, you will be notified immediately by email, so be sure to keep your Preferred Email Address in AMCAS updated!

We look forward to reviewing your application!

MD/PhD Information Sessions

MSTP Program Information Sessions (on Zoom)
We hold virtual information sessions about the MD/PhD Program to review the distinctive features that make Emory’s MD/PhD Program unique. We will also have time to address questions about the MD/PhD application process. Usually, these sessions occur in the spring, but occasionally other times are considered. 

Upcoming Emory MD/PhD Program Info Sessions
Tuesday, 6/2/26, 5-6pm EST
Wednesday, 6/10/26, noon-1pm EST
If you would like to be alerted to these sessions, please sign up here: Sign Up for MD/PhD Info Sessions

How to Apply
Step 1: Course Requirements
Step 2: Experiences
Step 3: MCAT
Step 4: AMCAS Application
Step 5: Letters of Recommendation
Step 6: Supplemental Application and Technical Standards
Application Review Process

All completed applications will remain in review until the end of the interview season (October – March). We cannot guarantee the time frame in which your application will be reviewed. No completed applicant will be rejected during the interview season and the ONLY decision that is made during this time is the decision to invite for an interview. If you are selected for an interview, you will be contacted by email or telephone.

It is extremely critical that you keep your contact information updated with AMCAS during this time. Please also let the Office of Admissions know if you will be out of the country or unreachable by telephone or email for any period of time during the interview season.

A personal interview is required to be considered for acceptance – there are no exceptions.

Criteria for Selection

Competitive applicants will present a superb level of scholarship and strong MCAT scores. Additional factors that are considered by our Admissions Committee include:  

personal motivation for pursuing a career in medicine
letters of recommendation
experience with patients and physicians in a clinical setting
leadership
extracurricular activities
service and involvement in community activities
potential barriers to resources and support
alignment with Emory’s mission

Schedule
Date and Time	Details
October 15 by 11:59 PM EST	Deadline to submit the AMCAS Application
December 1 by 11:59 PM EST	Deadline to submit the Emory Supplemental Application (including photo and application fee)
Deadline to submit all letters of recommendation online via the AMCAS Letter Service
March 1	Recommended deadline to submit FAFSA and PROFILE financial aid applications
April 30	Final decision deadline for students accepted to both the MD and the MD/PhD program (incoming students may hold only one acceptance to a medical school after this date)
June 1	Deadline to select “Plan-to-Enroll” at Emory School of Medicine via the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School tool, indicating that all acceptances to other medical schools have been withdrawn. Accepted students may continue to hold wait list spots at other medical schools until July 20.
July 20	Deadline to select "Commit to Enroll" at Emory School of Medicine on the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School tool, indicating that a final decision has been made about where to attend medical school and that all other acceptances and wait list spots have been withdrawn.


IMPORTANT NOTE: Due to the high volume of applications that we receive each year, we strongly recommend that you submit your applications (both the AMCAS application and the Emory Supplemental Application) EARLY. Early submission does not guarantee an interview, but it does place your application in review earlier. Please also note that no deadline extensions will be granted.

Types of Financial Aid
Scholarships for Medical Students

Nearly 70 scholarships are awarded by the Office of Financial Aid based on eligibility as determined by the information the student submits on the FAFSA and the PROFILE. No supplemental applications are required. This includes nearly 20 scholarships based on merit and several based on community service.  

All accepted students (regardless of citizenship or DACA status) are eligible for the same merit-based scholarships available to domestic students. No separate application is required.  All accepted students are automatically considered for merit-based awards.




Scholarships Based on Merit

Highlights

Robert W. Woodruff Fellowships

Six first-year medical students are selected as recipients of Woodruff Fellowships. Each fellowship covers full tuition and a stipend for a four-year period of study. Applicants are assessed on demonstrated qualities of forceful and unselfish character, intellectual and personal vigor, outstanding academic achievement, motivation for medicine, impressive communication skills, leadership, and creativity. A special application is not required. Individuals accepted to the initial class (through mid-March) will constitute the pool from which finalists will be selected. For additional information, contact the Office of Admissions of the School of Medicine.

Dr. G. Keith Pilling Scholarship

A four-year full tuition scholarship is awarded once every four years to a student with outstanding academic merit, financial need, and is a U.S. citizen.

Loan Programs

Direct Federal Unsubsidized Stafford Loan – Not based on financial need; up to $47,167 per academic year; 6.60% interest rate; interest is assessed as soon as student receives full disbursement of loan but student can allow interest to accumulate and accumulated interest is added to loan amount when student begins repayment; up to 10 years to repay (may be extended up to 25 years depending on total indebtedness); no cosigner required.
Direct Federal GradPLUS Loan – Not based on financial need; can borrow up to the cost of attendance (see below) minus any other aid student is receiving; 7.60% interest rate; repayment begins 60 days after student receives full disbursement of loan but student can request a deferment until 6 months after leaving school; interest accumulates if student defers payments while enrolled; up to 10 years to repay (may be extended up to 25 years depending on total indebtedness); student must pass a credit check or have a credit-worthy cosigner.

Tuition and Aid
We prioritize value and affordability

We understand the financial burden of continuing your education and obtaining your M.D. degree. We strive to create a student experience you won’t find elsewhere at an unbeatable value.

We want you to be able to choose a career based primarily on your interests, skills, and aptitudes rather than financial considerations due to student debt. Because of this, we offer a variety of scholarships, grants, and loans to reduce the burden of medical education.

2026-2027 tuition rates, fees, and other expenses

Estimated budget information is provided to allow you to completely prepare for your education. The estimated budget is the estimated cost of education-related expenses.

Student benefits

Students are offered low-cost comprehensive medical insurance, including a prescription drug plan, as well as dental and vision insurance. Other student benefits include access to subsidized gym memberships, counseling services, and many more resources offered by our Office of Student Financial Aid and Registrar.

Grants and Scholarships
Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine tuition scholarships

Through the generous gifts of Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine benefactors, medical school tuition scholarships are available. The Scholarship Committee makes these awards based on both merit and financial need. These awards are very competitive.

Scholarship eligibility is reviewed for all appointed students who apply for financial aid. Parental data is used in the evaluation of the financial need component of scholarship awards. These awards are renewable subject to continued meritorious performance. These awards may be adjusted if the student receives external funding equal to 100% of their cost of attendance.

Mayo Clinic Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences tuition waiver

All predoctoral (Ph.D.) students enrolled full-time in an eligible program at Mayo Clinic Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences are provided with a tuition waiver. This tuition waiver is equal to the amount of tuition charged for the specific term. The tuition waiver is provided as part of the appointment to Mayo Clinic Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences.

Mayo Clinic School of Health Sciences need-based scholarship and Federal Pell Grant

The need-based scholarship award program is designed to assist students in funding the cost of their education. The selection criterion for this award is based on a formula that evaluates student-documented financial need. Parental data is used in the evaluation of each scholarship award and recipient. These award amounts vary annually and are made possible by generous benefactor contributions to Mayo Clinic School of Health Sciences.

The Federal Pell Grant is based on financial need as determined by the information submitted on your Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). This grant program is available for undergraduate students only. Detailed information can be found on the Federal Pell Grants website

Admission
 
Welcome to Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine! Explore our MD programs:
University Program: A traditional four-year MD program offering an integrated curriculum to train well-rounded physicians grounded in clinical mastery, scientific inquiry, leadership, and professionalism.
Lerner College of Medicine Program: A five-year MD program in partnership with the Cleveland Clinic, focusing on training physician-investigators with a research-intensive curriculum.
Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP): An MD-PhD program designed for those aspiring to careers as physician-scientists, integrating medical education through the University Program with rigorous research training.

Get to know our team. 

Our Admissions Process

The goal of our admissions process is to further the mission of the Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine, which includes excellence in medical education, discoveries in translational science, and improving community health. To best meet the needs of the patient populations in Ohio and beyond and to achieve the goals of the institution, the School of Medicine's admissions process uses a balanced approach that considers all aspects of the application, including experiences, academic metrics, and personal attributes.

Are you planning a visit to the School of Medicine? Tour availability is dependent on staff capacity, and we typically can accommodate individual tour requests in the spring after the interview season has concluded. Please note that, out of fairness to all applicants, we are unable to provide tours to current applicants. For more information on the university, take a look at the University's Visitor Central.

If you’ve already applied to our program, please check your "Application Status" on your iApply account prior to calling. Application status checks by phone are intended for applicants with unusual and/or complicated circumstances. Admission personnel are prohibited from discussing any application or acceptance information with anyone other than the applicant.

### Funding Landscape & Program Orientations Summary

1. **Where Funding Support is Strongest:**
   - **Universal / Near-Universal Debt-Free Coverage:** **NYU Grossman** and **Case Western (CCLCM)** provide 100% tuition scholarships to every matriculated student as a baseline guarantee.
   - **Income-Tiered Full Rides:** **Johns Hopkins** offers comprehensive full cost of attendance (tuition, fees, and living expenses) for families making under $175,000/yr and free tuition for families under $300,000/yr. **Columbia Vagelos** meets 100% of demonstrated need with scholarships, eliminating all need-based loans.
   - **Large-Scale Endowed Tuition Aid:** **WashU** provides full tuition to over 71% of entering students, while **Vanderbilt** funds 68% of students with institutional aid (enabling nearly half to graduate with zero medical debt).

2. **Program Lean — Research vs. Leadership vs. Service:**
   - **Research-Leaning:** Approximately **60%** of the specialized programs emphasize scientific discovery and investigator training. Institutions like **Stanford (MedScholars)**, **Yale (OSR Fellowships)**, **Duke (Third Year)**, **UChicago (Summer Research Program)**, and **Case Western (CCLCM)** offer dedicated, multi-month to full-year stipends, protected curricular blocks, and tuition subsidies for laboratory or clinical research.
   - **Leadership & Merit-Leaning:** Approximately **25%** focus on identifying and developing future healthcare change agents. Notable examples include the **Emory Woodruff Fellowship**, **UPenn 21st Century Scholars**, and **UCLA Leaders of Tomorrow**, which award four-year full tuition plus research/living stipends to students demonstrating character, initiative, and high academic performance.
   - **Service & Equity-Leaning:** Approximately **15%** are targeted toward underserved care and structural equity. Programs like **UCSF PRIME-US** and **University of Washington WWAMI/TRUST** prepare physicians to serve urban underserved communities and rural healthcare deserts through longitudinal mentoring, community projects, and subsidized master's degrees.

### Top Recommendations: Where to Focus First

1. **Prioritize Universal & Large-Scale Need-Blind Full-Tuition Schools:**
   - Apply early to **NYU Grossman**, **Columbia Vagelos**, **Johns Hopkins**, **WashU**, and **Case Western (CCLCM)**. Because these institutions offer full tuition or 100% debt-free packages, gaining an admission offer here dramatically alters your financial horizon and eliminates loan repayment pressure.

2. **Align Target Schools with Your Curricular and Pacing Style:**
   - If you want **protected research time without stepping out into a 5th year**, prioritize **Duke** (accelerated 1-year basic science with 3rd-year research) or **Michigan** (Branches + Capstone for Impact).
   - If you thrive in a **high-autonomy, non-competitive learning environment**, focus on **Yale** (non-graded pre-clerkship with required investigative thesis).
   - If your passion is **urban underserved medicine or health equity**, focus on **UCSF (PRIME-US)** or **UCLA (PRIME-LA)**.

3. **Master the Early Timeline Window:**
   - Several top research programs have earlier submission deadlines than the national standard (e.g., **Michigan AMCAS is Sept. 15**; **Stanford, UW, UCLA, Mayo AMCAS are Oct. 1**; **Harvard, Hopkins, Columbia, UCSF, Penn, Duke, WashU, Case Western AMCAS are Oct. 15**).
   - Submit your AMCAS primary in late May/early June and return secondary applications within **10 to 14 days** of invitation. Most of these schools review and extend interview invitations on a rolling basis beginning in July and August.
